symptom: With the child declared `parameter $Task: M.Item`, the parent's `call workflow M.WF_Child(Task = $WorkflowContext);` passed `check --references` and `exec`, then mx check reported CE1613 "The selected parameter 'M.WF_Child.Task' no longer exists" (11.6.6 and 11.15.0); `mxcli syntax workflow call-workflow` taught that form with `(Request = $WorkflowContext)` (mendixlabs/mxcli#1530).
cause: buildCallWorkflowActivity writes the mapping key as <called workflow>.<key> verbatim, but a workflow has exactly one parameter and mxcli always stores it as WorkflowContext (the header's `$Task` is only an alias, see contextExprNormalizer). So any other key names a parameter that cannot exist, and nothing between the parser and the build compared the key against that fixed name.
file: mdl/executor/validate_workflow_call.go (MDL-WF18, wired into ValidateWorkflow, ValidateAlterWorkflow, execCreateWorkflow and execAlterWorkflow); cmd_workflows_write.go writes a casing variant as WorkflowContext; cmd/mxcli/syntax/features_workflow.go example
insight: The alias that makes `parameter $Task` work on the CHILD side is exactly what makes `Task = ` look right on the CALLER side: the author sees the name they declared and reuses it. Where a name is an alias for a fixed stored name, every place that writes a reference to it needs the same alias table or a refusal - grep for the stored constant (workflowContextVar) and check each writer. Refused rather than renamed: a key naming some other parameter is a misunderstanding worth stating, and the wrong syntax-help example would otherwise keep teaching it. Measured: the repro is CE1613 on 11.6.6 and 11.15.0; the same child header with the key `WorkflowContext` is 0 errors on both.
